walkthrough: The rods are frictionless, so tension is transmitted unchanged. The force pulling up-left on the knot equals $F_1$ and the force pulling up-right equals $F_2$.
At the knot three forces act in equilibrium: $F_1$ along the left cord, $F_2$ along the right cord with $90^{\circ}$ between them, and $10 \text{ N}$ vertically down from the object.
For equilibrium the vector sum of $F_1$ and $F_2$ must be $10 \text{ N}$ vertically up. Because they are perpendicular, Pythagoras gives $\sqrt{F_1^2+F_2^2}=10 \text{ N}$.
Test the numbers: $\sqrt{6.0^2+8.0^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10 \text{ N}$, while $\sqrt{4.0^2+6.0^2} \approx 7.2 \text{ N}$. Only the 6.0 N and 8.0 N pair works.

Choose the order from horizontal equilibrium. The left cord is more horizontal than the right cord, so $F_1 \sin\phi_1 = F_2 \sin\phi_2$ requires the larger angle $\phi_1$ to pair with the smaller tension. Hence $F_1=6.0 \text{ N}$ and $F_2=8.0 \text{ N}$. This is option C.
